questions.question: Assess the effectiveness of intervention planning for OCD and personality disorders. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Assess the effectiveness of intervention planning for OCD and personality
  • disorders.
  • Effectiveness of Intervention Planning for OCD
  • a) Use of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) helps modify obsessive thoughts.
  • b) Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is highly effective in reducing compulsions.
  • c) Combination with medication (SSRIs) improves outcomes.
  • d) Structured planning ensures gradual symptom reduction.
  • e) Involvement of family improves treatment adherence.
  • f) Regular monitoring helps in adjusting treatment strategies.
  • g) Limitation: Some patients show relapse or resistance to treatment.
  • Effectiveness of Intervention Planning for Personality Disorders
  • a) Focus on long-term psychotherapy (e.g., DBT, CBT).
  • b) Helps in improving emotional regulation and behaviour control.
  • c) Promotes better interpersonal relationships.
  • d) Individualized planning addresses specific personality traits.
  • e) Encourages self-awareness and coping skills.
  • f) Limitation: Progress is often slow and requires long-term commitment.
  • g) Resistance to change may reduce effectiveness.
  • Overall Assessment
  • Intervention planning is effective when it is individualized, multidisciplinary, and continuous, but its
  • success depends on patient motivation, severity of disorder, and quality of implementation.
  • -[E] / [CO5]
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  •  Individualized care planning- Help tailor treatment plans according to patient circumstances.
  •  Coordination with healthcare team- Work with doctors, nurses, and therapists for integrated care.
  •  Facilitating communication- Explain treatment plans clearly to patients and families.
  •  Counselling and emotional support- Help patients cope with illness and stress.
  •  Ensuring treatment adherence- Motivate patients to follow prescribed therapies and medications.
  •  Resource mobilization- Link patients to financial aid, welfare schemes, and community resources.
  •  Advocacy- Protect patient rights and ensure access to quality care.
  •  Family involvement- Engage family members in care and support systems.
  •  Crisis intervention- Address emergencies and sudden psychological distress.
  •  Monitoring progress - Track patient response to treatment and suggest modifications.
  •  Rehabilitation support- Assist in reintegration into family and society.
  •  Health education- Provide awareness about disease, prevention, and care.
  •  Addressing social barriers- Tackle stigma, poverty, and environmental factors affecting treatment.
  •  Follow-up and continuity of care- Ensure long-term support and prevent relapse.
  • -[E] / [CO6]

questions.question: Analyze the relevance of Social Psychiatry and evaluate its effectiveness. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the relevance of Social Psychiatry and evaluate its effectiveness. –
  • Relevance of Social Psychiatry
  • a) Recognizes the impact of social determinants (poverty, unemployment, inequality) on mental
  • health.
  • b) Emphasizes community-based care rather than institutionalization.
  • c) Promotes preventive approaches to mental illness.
  • d) Addresses stigma and discrimination associated with mental disorders.
  • e) Considers family and cultural influences in treatment.
  • f) Encourages holistic understanding of mental health (biological + social + psychological).
  • g) Supports integration of mental health into primary healthcare.
  • h) Focuses on rehabilitation and social reintegration.
  • Effectiveness of Social Psychiatry
  • a) Improves access to mental health services at the community level.
  • b) Enhances early identification and intervention.
  • c) Reduces hospitalization and institutional dependence.
  • d) Strengthens family and community support systems.
  • An] / [CO5]

questions.question: Discuss the dimensions of health and analyse their interrelationship / [CO1] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the dimensions of health and analyse their interrelationship
  • Dimensions of Health
  • a) Physical health - Refers to proper functioning of the body and absence of illness.
  • b) Mental health- Involves emotional stability, coping ability, and psychological well-being.
  • c) Social health- Ability to form satisfying relationships and adapt to social environments.
  • d) Emotional health - Capacity to express and manage feelings effectively.
  • e) Spiritual health- Relates to values, beliefs, and sense of purpose in life.
  • f) Environmental health- Impact of surroundings like sanitation, pollution, and living conditions.
  • g) Occupational health - Balance between work and personal life, job satisfaction, and safety.
  • Interrelationship among Dimensions
  • a) Holistic nature- All dimensions are interconnected and influence each other.
  • b) Physical–mental link- Poor physical health can lead to stress; mental illness can affect physical
  • well-being.
  • c) Mental–emotional connection- Emotional stability supports mental health.
  • d) Social influence on mental health -Strong relationships improve psychological well-being.
  • e) Environmental impact -Healthy surroundings promote physical and mental health.
  • f) Occupational influence- Job stress can affect mental and physical health.
  • g) Spiritual support- Spiritual well-being helps in coping with stress and illness.
  • h) Balance leads to overall well-being -Proper integration of all dimensions ensures a healthy and
  • productive life.
  • [An] / [CO1
